Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered in this aromatic gravy, creating a dish that is both comforting and exquisitely flavorful. It is a perfect balance of tangy, sweet, and subtly spicy notes, making it a universally adored Indian classic.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, turmeric powder, Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2 hours in the refrigerator for deeper flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon cooking oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until the chicken is browned on all sides and cooked through, which typically takes about 8-10 minutes. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and set it aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add 2 tablespoons of butter. Once the butter has melted, add the finely chopped onion and sauté until it becomes translucent and soft, approximately 5-7 minutes. Then, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger garlic paste and cook for another minute until it becomes fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree, the soaked cashews, coriander powder, cumin powder, and a pinch of salt. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then cover the pan and let it cook for 10-12 minutes. This step allows the flavors to meld beautifully and the tomatoes to soften further.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Gravy
instructions.text: Allow the gravy mixture to cool slightly before transferring it to a blender. Blend until it achieves a very smooth consistency. For an extra silky and refined butter chicken gravy, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, discarding any coarse solids.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, sugar, and the crushed kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) to the strained gravy. Bring it to a gentle simmer, stirring constantly. Stir in the previously cooked chicken pieces and the heavy cream. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, allowing the chicken to fully absorb the rich and creamy flavors of the gravy.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Taste the Butter Chicken and adjust the seasoning if needed, adding more salt or sugar to balance the flavors to your preference. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with warm naan bread, roti, or fluffy basmati rice for a complete and satisfying Indian lunch.

tips: For an authentic smoky flavor, you can char the cooked chicken slightly on a grill or under a broiler before adding it to the gravy.
Soaking cashews before blending is crucial for a smooth, creamy gravy. If you dont have cashews, almonds or a teaspoon of cornstarch slurry can be used as a thickener.
Butter Chicken tastes even better the next day as the flavors deepen. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: A Quintessential Indian Lunch Delight

Few dishes evoke the warmth and comfort of Indian cuisine quite like Butter Chicken. Known traditionally as Murgh Makhani, this iconic curry has charmed palates worldwide with its rich, creamy texture, subtly spiced tomato gravy, and succulent pieces of tender chicken. While often reserved for special dinners, Butter Chicken makes for an incredibly satisfying and remarkably achievable Indian lunch recipe, perfect for brightening any midday meal. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a culinary novice, mastering this classic dish at home is a rewarding experience that promises a burst of authentic Indian flavors. Get ready to dive into the history, ingredients, and step-by-step process of creating your very own delectable Murgh Makhani.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

At its heart, Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a culinary masterpiece born in the bustling kitchens of Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, India, during the 1950s. The story goes that leftover tandoori chicken was simmered in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream, creating a dish so revolutionary it quickly became a national treasure. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly describing its luxurious base. This dish is characterized by its vibrant orange-red hue, a result of ripe tomatoes and a touch of Kashmiri chili powder, which provides color without excessive heat. The gravy is famously smooth, often pureed to achieve a velvety consistency, and infused with aromatic spices like garam masala, fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), and sometimes a hint of sweetness. It's the ultimate comfort food, offering a harmonious balance of tangy, sweet, and savory notes that dance on the palate.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken requires a combination of fresh ingredients and aromatic spices. Here’s what you’ll need for a truly unforgettable Murgh Makhani:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 medium fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, optional)
*   1/2 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (adjust to taste)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1 tablespoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create a delicious Murgh Makhani that will impress everyone at the lunch table:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to meld and the chicken to tenderize.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, melt the butter along with the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the crushed/pureed tomatoes, soaked cashews (if using), red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes soften and the mixture thickens slightly.

4.  **Blend the Gravy:** Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, you can pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is crucial for achieving the signature smoothness of Murgh Makhani.

5.  **Finish the Gravy:** Return the smooth gravy to the pan. Add the sugar and bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed kasuri methi. Continue to simmer for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the gravy to thicken to your desired consistency. Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed.

6.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken thoroughly. Cook for another 5 minutes to ensure the chicken absorbs the flavors of the rich gravy. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving your exquisite Butter Chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken is all about paying attention to a few key details:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal for maximum flavor infusion.
*   **Quality Tomatoes:** Use good quality canned crushed tomatoes or ripe, fresh tomatoes. They form the backbone of the gravy, so their flavor is paramount.
*   **Smooth Gravy:** Blending the gravy until absolutely smooth is non-negotiable for authentic Murgh Makhani. Straining it afterwards ensures there are no fibrous bits, resulting in a luxurious, velvety texture.
*   **Kasuri Methi Magic:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) are essential. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their aromatic oils; they lend a distinctive, slightly bitter, and sweet aroma that is characteristic of Butter Chicken.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste and adjust the balance of sweet, tangy, and spicy. A touch of sugar can balance the acidity of the tomatoes, while a little extra cream can mellow the heat.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of Indian breads and rice. For a truly authentic Indian lunch experience, serve your Murgh Makhani with:

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, fluffy, and slightly charred naan is perfect for scooping up the rich gravy. Garlic naan or butter naan elevate the experience.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Whole wheat flatbreads like roti or flaky paratha also make excellent accompaniments.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Aromatic basmati rice, either plain or as jeera rice (cumin rice), provides a comforting base to soak up all the delicious flavors.
*   **Side Salad or Raita:** A simple cucumber and onion salad or a cooling cucumber raita (yogurt dip) can cut through the richness of the curry, offering a refreshing contrast.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, you can explore several variations and substitutions to suit dietary needs or personal preferences:

*   **Dairy-Free Murgh Makhani:** For a dairy-free version, substitute yogurt with a plant-based alternative, use a plant-based butter, and replace heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream for similar richness.
*   **Vegetarian Butter Chicken:** Easily transform this into Paneer Makhani by replacing chicken with cubed paneer (Indian cheese). Simply pan-fry the paneer until golden before adding it to the gravy. Tofu can also be used for a vegan option.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For more heat, use regular chili powder; for vibrant color with mild heat, stick to Kashmiri chili powder.
*   **Smoking the Chicken:** For an authentic tandoor-like flavor, you can give your cooked chicken a charcoal smoke. Heat a small piece of charcoal until red hot, place it in a small bowl inside the curry, drizzle a little ghee over it, and quickly cover the pot for a few minutes. This infuses the Butter Chicken with a smoky aroma.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a meal; it's an experience. Its creamy texture and complex flavors make it a beloved choice for any occasion, especially as a comforting and satisfying Indian lunch. By following this detailed guide, you can recreate this iconic dish in your own kitchen, bringing the taste of India right to your table. Enjoy the process, savor the aromas, and delight in every spoonful of your homemade Murgh Makhani!
